A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Frame Guidance work. Their text, figures, tables, algorithms, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite reformatting, renumbering, and additions.

before.justification: V1 reports original generation experiments, quantitative comparisons, human evaluations, memory measurements, and ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds memory-scaling measurements, a stage-boundary ablation, rapid-motion tests, and additional qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: The latent-slicing and VLO framework remains intact. Section 4.4 removes the stop-gradient on the first frame in the looping loss. Algorithm 3 also moves flow-matching guidance from before re-noising to afterward, changing its effective scaling, although Appendix C.3 retains the earlier explanation.

E1.justification: DAVIS, Pexels, and the 54-prompt stylization benchmark are retained. V2 adds joint style-and-loop generation, examples labeled as OOD styles, Sobel-edge control scenarios, and accelerated-motion tests, extending conditions within the existing video-generation tasks.

E2.justification: The main keyframe and stylization comparator sets are unchanged. V2 adds a shortcut/no-denoising-network comparator to the gradient-influence experiment in Figure 4(c); v1 Figure 4(d) displayed only the proposed method. Shortcut failure examples already existed in v1 Appendix C.4.

E3.justification: New protocols include a stage-boundary sweep over 20 DAVIS videos, memory measurements with one, two, or four guided frames using RGB/depth losses, and motion acceleration through temporal subsampling. Existing benchmark preprocessing, human-study sizes, and inference-budget limits are retained.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands diagnostic coverage: stage-boundary sensitivity, memory scaling across guidance configurations, temporal locality under accelerated motion, matched-seed style/content comparisons, and explicit OOD-style and edge-control failures. These supplement the retained optimization-strategy, sliced-reconstruction, and shortcut analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix B.1 newly states that all comparisons used the same random seed, also emphasized in Figure 17. This adds seed-matching information without establishing additional runs. Existing human-evaluation error bars remain, with no new confidence-interval or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: Figures 6 and 8 and Table 1 retain their scores, but v2 substantially expands supplementary results. Figure 26 reports lowest FVD 514.47 at tE=6 and lowest FID 56.18 at tE=8 in its separate 20-video study. Table 2 adds memory measurements, while new figures report motion robustness, compositional generation, and failure outcomes.

T1.justification: The formal looping-loss definition in Section 4.4 drops the stop-gradient operator, changing its specified differentiation rule. The background diffusion and flow-matching equations and derivations remain otherwise unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central claims remain training-free, model-agnostic frame-level control using latent slicing and VLO across diverse applications. V2's added abstract statement about controlling entire videos through selected frames reiterates a claim already present in v1.

C2.justification: V2 supplements the existing computational-cost and base-model limitations with concrete OOD-style failures and unreliable fine-grained edge control, identifying trained methods as an alternative. Appendix C.6 newly interprets temporal locality as architecture-driven and largely independent of motion speed.

D1.justification: V2 adds a source-code repository link and reproducibility statement, explains sliced-latent indexing more explicitly, and discloses a 20%-of-initial layout-distance criterion for selecting the early-stage boundary. Existing hardware, principal hyperparameters, checkpointing, and downsampling details are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds TokenFlow, Text2Video-Zero, Tune-A-Video, ControlVideo, and FreeInit, while removing Motion Prompting. It now credits FreeInit when discussing early layout formation. These are limited positioning changes; the central distinction from task-specific or training-dependent methods remains.

P1.justification: V2 makes focused rewrites to the VLO and gradient-propagation explanations, renames stage terminology, moves limitations into the main text, and adds acknowledgment, reproducibility, and LLM-use statements. Most prose and the overall section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands and revises the visual presentation: Figures 3–4 are redrawn, Figure 9 gains a combined-control example, and new failure, memory, sensitivity, and rapid-motion displays are added. The earlier layout-analysis plots reappear in Figure 26, and the algorithm panels are reorganized and expanded.

improvement.justification: The added sensitivity, memory-scaling, rapid-motion, and failure analyses better support and bound the existing method, while the code-access statement and implementation explanations improve reproducibility. The main benchmark evidence remains unchanged. These provide a limited net improvement, tempered by the unresolved inconsistency between revised Algorithm 3 and Appendix C.3's description of the flow-matching update.
